archetype.name: Pocket Passer (vertical)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower from the pocket who wins with accuracy and willingness to push the ball past the sticks, not with his legs. He holds the ball long enough to let routes develop and pays for it in sacks.

report.headline: Bolder and cleaner downfield; holding the ball still costs him on money downs
report.take:
Stroud's career has swung hard: a sharp rookie year (8.23 yards per attempt, 6th), a 2024 slide to -0.007 EPA per play with 12 interceptions, and a 2025 recovery that came without much accuracy (bad-throw rate ranked 48th of 63). The 2026 version is the most aggressive and cleanest he has been. His aggressive-throw rate is 19.18%, up 6.4 points from last year. His bad-throw rate fell to 11.4%, 10th of 37 and 5.4 points better than 2025. His CPOE of 5.25 (10th) compares with 0.4 a year ago. He is averaging 285.7 passing yards a game, 4th in the league, a 4,856-yard pace.

The value comes almost entirely downfield. Throws of 10+ air yards have added 42.6 EPA, against 16.5 on everything shorter. Deep balls run at 0.604 EPA per attempt with a 10.3 CPOE, which is real downfield accuracy rather than lucky completions. The quick game behind the line has been a sinkhole at -9.2 EPA on those throws, which reflects screen design and blocking as much as the quarterback. The targets split cleanly too. Nico Collins (0.797 per target) and Jaylin Noel (0.956) have carried the efficiency. Xavier Hutchinson has drawn 34 targets at essentially zero EPA. Houston's defense ranks 30th in explosive pass rate allowed, which has produced shootouts with Buffalo, Dallas and Jacksonville. The offense still passes about as often as the situation predicts (-0.4 over expected), so the yardage is not purely game script.

The season EPA per dropback (0.136, 18th) understates how well he is playing now, and it also masks two real problems. The first three games were flat. Against Cincinnati he went 30-for-55 for 353 yards but -6.4 EPA, a case of volume without efficiency. The last three have been outstanding: 0.384 EPA per dropback, a 12.2 CPOE and 9.29 yards per attempt. That run came against Dallas (31st-ranked defense today), Tennessee (22nd) and Jacksonville (17th), so discount it somewhat. Two problems persist underneath:
- **Third down:** EPA is -0.028, with 7 sacks on 58 plays and an average of 8.4 yards to go.
- **Pressure-to-sack rate:** 32.6%, 27th of 37. It matches his 2023-24 rates (0.309, 0.299), which makes last year's 0.221 look like the outlier, not the new normal.

The red zone has yielded 8 touchdowns despite -0.133 EPA, with 4 sacks in there. A 0.5% interception rate is also unlikely to hold, since he already has three turnover-worthy fumbles.

The improvements that matter most should stick, because they are process stats: fewer bad throws and more intent downfield. The touchdown-free interception luck and the last-three heater will cool. Tank Dell's expected return is the swing piece. If Dell absorbs Hutchinson's dead-weight targets, the per-play efficiency has room to hold near the top-12 level even as the opponents get tougher.

strengths.title: Accurate, aggressive intermediate-to-deep passing
strengths.body: His EPA comes from throws past 10 yards, and the deep shots land at an accuracy rate well above expectation. He is throwing into tight windows more often than last year and missing far less. That combination is driven by skill rather than opponents, and it has held in both his good and bad games.

strengths.title: Bad-throw rate finally fixed
strengths.body: For three seasons his bad-throw rate ranked near the bottom of the league. Now it sits 10th of 37. Along with the jump in CPOE, this is the clearest sign the season is a real step and not just volume. Charting stats like this are fairly sticky once they move this much.

strengths.title: Recent form at a top level
strengths.body: Over the last three games he has produced 0.384 EPA per dropback with a 3.9% sack rate. The sack rate is the more encouraging part, since it suggests the ball is coming out on time. The opponents were soft, so treat this as his ceiling rather than his baseline.

concerns.title: Sacks kill drives on key downs
concerns.body: A pressure-to-sack rate of 32.6% matches his first two seasons, so this is who he is rather than a slump. It is partly the price of holding the ball for the downfield throws. It shows up worst on third down, where 7 sacks drag his EPA below zero despite a high completion rate over expected.

concerns.title: Dead targets and a broken quick game
concerns.body: Hutchinson's 34 targets have added nothing, and throws behind the line have lost 9.2 EPA. Both are mostly roster and scheme problems rather than Stroud's. They still cap his floor in games where the deep shots aren't there.

concerns.title: Turnover luck will turn
concerns.body: One interception on 219 attempts is far below anything in his career, which includes 12 picks in 2024. He already has three turnover-worthy fumbles. Expect the interception rate to drift toward a normal level.

trend.note: The season split into a flat first three weeks (negative passing EPA in Weeks 2 and 3) and a strong last three (15.2, 10.5 and 13.9 EPA). The rise lines up with softer defenses but also with cleaner pockets and fewer bad throws.

nextGame.headline: No pass rush to punish his holding; volume is the question
nextGame.body:
The Giants are nearly the ideal opponent for his biggest weakness. They rank 31st in hit rate and 30th in sack rate, so the long-developing throws he likes should come with time. The defense is 22nd in pass EPA and allows 2.5 quarterback touchdowns a game (27th). The catch is that it is stingy where Stroud makes his money. It ranks 2nd against deep passes and 5th in passing yards allowed to quarterbacks. It also allows little to tight ends, which squeezes Dalton Schultz.

Availability on the Giants' side favors him. Safety Tyler Nubin (83% of snaps) and corner Colton Hood are out, and starting corner Greg Newsome II (concussion) and every-down linebacker Tremaine Edmunds are questionable. That is a thinned back seven against Collins and Noel downfield. For Houston, Tank Dell is on track to debut, which could finally replace Hutchinson's empty targets. David Montgomery is out, leaving a run game already 22nd in EPA without its lead back. As a 10-point favorite against a run funnel, Houston may lean on the ground with a lead, which caps his attempts in a modest 42.5 total.

keyMatchups.title: Clean pockets against a soft rush
keyMatchups.body: His sacks come from holding the ball, and the Giants rarely get home. If the rush stays this quiet, his third-down and red-zone drives should stop dying on sacks.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots against a strong deep defense
keyMatchups.body: His best area meets the Giants' best area. With Nubin out and two corners hurt, that deep resistance may not hold at full strength. It is still the main reason to expect efficient rather than huge yardage.

keyMatchups.title: Collins favored, Schultz squeezed
keyMatchups.body: Opposing WR1s have outscored their averages against this defense, while tight ends have been held well under. Expect the targets to tilt toward Collins and the receivers rather than Schultz.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dell takes Hutchinson's routes, and whether Houston keeps throwing once it leads with Montgomery out.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect a quarterback who stays clearly above last year without matching the last three weeks. The accuracy and aggressiveness gains look like real changes in how he is playing, and Dell's return should upgrade the weakest part of the target tree. What regresses:
- **Interceptions:** the near-zero rate will rise.
- **Efficiency:** the last-three EPA will slide back toward the low-to-mid 0.2s once tougher defenses appear.
- **Sacks:** they will keep taxing him on third down, because that has been true his whole career.

Houston's leaky pass defense should keep producing high-volume games. Projected per-game ranges for the rest of the season:
- Passing yards: 255–300
- Passing TDs: 1.4–2.1
- Interceptions: 0.3–0.6
- Rushing yards: 8–18
swingFactors: Sack rate on third down against real pass rushes

confidence.note: Six games, with the hot stretch against weak defenses. The process gains (bad throws, CPOE) support a real step forward.
